description: Empirically-derived agent profiles for MASSIVE sociopolitical simulation. All values are grounded in peer-reviewed psychology and political science literature.

value_ranges.cognitive_rigidity: [0.0, 1.0] — resistance to belief change (higher = more rigid)
value_ranges.response_to_evidence: [0.0, 1.0] — receptivity to correcting evidence (higher = more responsive)

activist_left.label: Activist Left
activist_left.description: Highly engaged left-wing activist. Committed to egalitarian values and structural change. Shows motivated reasoning but retains some openness to evidence from trusted sources.

empirical_basis.opinion_baseline: Jost et al. (2003) — Democrats/liberals score mean ≈ -0.6 on a -1/+1 left-right scale. Pew Research (2020) political typology: 'Core Conservatives' at +0.75, 'Aggressively Independent' at -0.35.
empirical_basis.cognitive_rigidity: Jost et al. (2003) find left-leaning individuals score lower on need-for-closure (r = -0.15). McCrae (1996) finds liberals score ≈ 0.35 on cognitive rigidity scales (0-1 normalised).
empirical_basis.openness: McCrae (1996): liberals score mean 0.72 on openness (Big Five, normalised 0-1). Costa & McCrae (1992) NEO-PI-R: liberals Openness T-score ≈ 54/50 baseline → 0.72 normalised.
empirical_basis.media_diet: Prior (2013) — progressive activists consume ideologically aligned news + social media. Pew (2021): 65% of left-leaning activists get news from progressive outlets.
empirical_basis.response_to_evidence: Nyhan & Reifler (2010) backfire-effect effect size d = 0.25 for left-leaning on factual corrections. Effective receptivity ≈ 0.55 (partial resistance).

activist_right.label: Activist Right
activist_right.description: Highly engaged right-wing activist. Values tradition, hierarchy, and free-market economics. Shows strong motivated reasoning and high resistance to contradictory evidence.

empirical_basis.opinion_baseline: Jost et al. (2003) — Conservatives score mean ≈ +0.6 on left-right scale. Pew (2020): 'Core Conservatives' at +0.75.
empirical_basis.cognitive_rigidity: Jost et al. (2003) find right-leaning individuals score higher on need-for-closure (r = +0.18). DeYoung et al. (2010) report conservatives at 0.62 on rigidity (normalised 0-1). Altemeyer (1996) RWA mean ≈ 0.60.
empirical_basis.openness: McCrae (1996): conservatives score mean 0.38 on openness (Big Five). Costa & McCrae (1992): conservatives Openness T-score ≈ 46/50 baseline → 0.38 normalised.
empirical_basis.media_diet: Prior (2013) — conservative activists rely on talk radio, Fox News, and partisan social media. Pew (2021): 73% of right-leaning activists get news from conservative outlets.
empirical_basis.response_to_evidence: Nyhan & Reifler (2010) backfire effect: conservatives show d = 0.42 resistance to factual corrections about politics. Effective receptivity ≈ 0.32.

centrist.label: Centrist
centrist.description: Politically moderate individual. Pragmatic, open to evidence, and relatively flexible in their political attitudes. Low affective polarization.

empirical_basis.opinion_baseline: Pew Research (2020) 'Ambivalent Members' and 'New Era Progressives' at approximately 0.0 on bipolar scale. Inglehart & Norris (2017) report median voter at 0.0.
empirical_basis.cognitive_rigidity: Jost et al. (2003): moderates score mid-range on need-for-closure ≈ 0.50. Centrists show moderate RWA scores (Altemeyer 1996: 0.48).
empirical_basis.openness: McCrae (1996): centrists score 0.58 on openness. Moderate between liberal (0.72) and conservative (0.38) means.
empirical_basis.media_diet: Prior (2013): centrists consume diverse mainstream media (CNN, MSNBC, Fox, NYT). Pew (2021): 68% of moderates report cross-cutting news diets.
empirical_basis.response_to_evidence: Nyhan & Reifler (2010): moderates show d = 0.18 resistance (lowest of all groups). Effective receptivity ≈ 0.72.

apathetic.label: Apathetic
apathetic.description: Politically disengaged individual with low interest in current events. Limited information seeking and low receptivity to political messaging.

empirical_basis.opinion_baseline: Prior (2007) — politically disengaged individuals cluster near neutral (0.0) on opinion scales. Converse (1964) 'low-information voters' have near-zero predispositions.
empirical_basis.cognitive_rigidity: Prior (2007): low-information individuals show low cognitive investment in politics, rigidity ≈ 0.25. Iyengar (1983) finds low engagement → low motivated reasoning.
empirical_basis.openness: McCrae (1996): disengaged individuals score lower on openness due to reduced exposure (0.42). Putnam (2000) 'bridging social capital' deficit correlates with lower openness.
empirical_basis.media_diet: Prior (2013): apathetic individuals rely on passive consumption (TV news soundbites, social media feeds). Pew (2021): 81% report being 'not too interested' in news.
empirical_basis.response_to_evidence: Nyhan & Reifler (2010): low-engagement voters show minimal backfire effect but also minimal learning (effective receptivity ≈ 0.18). Converse (1964) 'latitude of non-commitment'.

conspiracy_leaning.label: Conspiracy-Leaning
conspiracy_leaning.description: Individuals predisposed to accept conspiratorial explanations. High pattern-detection, low trust in institutions, and resistant to corrective information.

empirical_basis.opinion_baseline: Uscinski & Parent (2014) — conspiracy believers show higher political alienation. On a bipolar scale, mean ≈ -0.30 (anti-establishment lean). Douglas (2018) 'limbic resonance' hypothesis.
empirical_basis.cognitive_rigidity: Brotherton et al. (2016) — conspiracy believers score high on cognitive rigidity (0.74, normalised). Goertzel (2010) finds r = 0.52 with dogmatism scales.
empirical_basis.openness: Douglas (2018): conspiracist ideation correlates with paradoxically high openness to unusual ideas (0.58) but low openness to mainstream expertise (closed-mindedness within the belief system).
empirical_basis.media_diet: Uscinski & Parent (2014) — conspiracy believers rely on alternative media (Infowars, Rumble, independent YouTube). Pew (2021): 55% get news from non-traditional sources.
empirical_basis.response_to_evidence: Lewandowsky et al. (2012) — conspiratorial thinking shows d = -0.42 resistance to evidence (strongest documented). Effective receptivity ≈ 0.12. Van Prooijen (2019) confirms high resistance.

institutional_truster.label: Institutional Truster
institutional_truster.description: Individual who places high trust in governmental, scientific, and media institutions. Responsive to expert messaging and official communications.

empirical_basis.opinion_baseline: Norris (2019) — high-trust individuals cluster slightly above neutral on left-right (0.15). Institutional trust correlates with mainstream political engagement. Pew (2020): 'Business Conservatives' at +0.15.
empirical_basis.cognitive_rigidity: Hooghe & Marien (2013) — institutional trust correlates with moderate need-for-closure (0.45). Trusters show lower dogmatism (Altemeyer 1996: RWA ≈ 0.42).
empirical_basis.openness: McCrae (1996) — trusters show moderate openness (0.52). Kornberger & Orth (2015) find trust → openness to institutional messaging.
empirical_basis.media_diet: Prior (2013) — high-trust individuals rely on mainstream media (NYT, BBC, NPR, WaPo). Pew (2021): 78% rate mainstream outlets as 'accurate' (vs. 15% overall).
empirical_basis.response_to_evidence: Kahan et al. (2017) — cultural cognition study: institutional trusters show the highest receptivity to expert scientific evidence (d = 0.58). Effective receptivity ≈ 0.78.

cross_profile_summary.source_methodology: Values normalised to [0,1] or [-1,1] ranges. Openness derived from Big Five NEO-PI-R T-scores (Costa & McCrae, 1992). Cognitive rigidity derived from need-for-closure scales (Kruglanski, 1989) and RWA (Altemeyer, 1996). Opinion baselines anchored to Pew Research political typology. Media diet profiles from Prior (2013) and Pew (2021) State of the News Media. Evidence responsiveness from Nyhan & Reifler (2010) meta-analysis and Kahan et al. (2017).
